<thought>
Perfect! This confirms my hypothesis:

1. When Ba(NO3)2 was added to the acidic sample (containing H2PO4⁻), no precipitate formed because Ba3(PO4)2 is soluble in acidic conditions.

2. When KOH was added to make the solution basic, a white precipitate formed. In basic conditions, H2PO4⁻ is converted to PO4³⁻, which then precipitates with Ba²⁺ to form Ba3(PO4)2 (white precipitate).

This behavior is characteristic of phosphate/dihydrogen phosphate and confirms that the anion is H2PO4⁻.

If it were HSO4⁻, the white BaSO4 precipitate would have formed immediately in the first test (acidic conditions), and adding base wouldn't change anything since BaSO4 is insoluble in both acidic and basic conditions.

Therefore, the anion in the sample is H2PO4⁻ (dihydrogen phosphate).

The complete salt is Sr(H2PO4)2 - strontium dihydrogen phosphate.
</thought>
